findings.description: In the required-permission loop, `rule_key "$perm"` is called as a bare simple command. `rule_key` returns 1 for any rule that is not of the form `Bash(...)`, and the script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. The allow/deny ingestion loops guard this with `|| continue`, acknowledging that non-Bash rules exist, but the required-list loop does not. The replaced `base_pattern_of` never failed, so this is a new abort path.
findings.failure_mode: If `all_required` contains any non-Bash rule (e.g. `Read`, `WebFetch(domain:...)`, `mcp__*`), the preflight checker exits 1 silently mid-loop with no report, no `--json` output, and no missing/denied summary; every caller treating a non-zero exit as 'permissions missing' now fails on every preflight.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the call: `rule_key "$perm" || { missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; }` (or handle non-Bash requirements by exact-string lookup), and add a bats case with a non-Bash required rule.

findings.description: `base="*${key#\*}"; base="${base%% *}"` assumes the requirement key begins with `*`. For an exact required rule (key `=git status`) the result is `*=git status` → `*=git`, a key that can never exist in `allow_by`/`deny_by`. Under the old `base_pattern_of`, an exact requirement `Bash(git status)` was still covered by an allow `Bash(git:*)`.
findings.failure_mode: Any exact-form requirement is reported as missing even when a base wildcard allow covers it, and a base wildcard deny on it is not detected (deny no longer wins).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the base from the body regardless of marker: `b="${key#[*=]}"; base="*${b%% *}"`.

findings.description: Authoritative mode is now selected only when `yq` is installed and `.loa.config.yaml` is present. If an operator sets `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` on a host without `yq`, the hook silently runs heuristic mode with no warning or audit event. The removed code emitted a `compliance.mode.change` audit line on downgrade; the replacement emits nothing. The `.run/.compliance-mode` cache file is also no longer written, so any other script that reads it (e.g. status reporting) sees a stale or absent value.
findings.failure_mode: Silent downgrade of the gate's mode on hosts lacking `yq`; stale `.compliance-mode` consumers report the pre-cycle-126 mode indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: When the config file exists but `yq` is missing, emit a stderr WARN and an audit.jsonl event; grep for other readers of `.run/.compliance-mode` and remove or re-point them.

findings.description: The new entry's comment cites the vendor page: 'Claude 4.6 and later models … include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing', and on that basis omits a `long_context` tier. The unchanged Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5 / Fable 5.1 entries still carry `long_context: {threshold_tokens: 200000, input_multiplier: 2.0, output_multiplier: 1.5, verified: false}`, and `test_five_family_declares_the_beta_header_list_and_the_long_context_tier` pins that. The catalog now asserts two contradictory pricing models for the same vendor statement.
findings.failure_mode: Metering over-charges Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable requests above 200K input by 2× (or under-charges Opus 5.5 if the older tier is correct); cost ceilings and budget gates derived from pricing are inconsistent across the family.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the `long_context` tiers from the FIVE_FAMILY entries (and update the test) with the same 2026-10-05 citation, or document why 5.5 alone is exempt.

findings.description: The diff adds the Opus 5.5 entry with `ceiling_calibration.source: conservative_default`, `calibrated_at: null`, and the test asserts exactly that. The supplied full-file context for this test module (apparently a later revision) contains `test_a_foreign_transport_calibration_carries_its_provenance` and `test_lookup_returns_the_concrete_bound_through_the_gate_path`, both of which require `claude-opus-5-5` to be calibrated with `method: probed_headless` and `measured_input_tokens`. Against the catalog as written in this diff, those tests fail.
findings.failure_mode: If the full-file tests are what runs in CI, the suite is red on the uncalibrated 5.5 entry; if the diff's tests are current, the review context is stale and the ceiling provenance of 5.5 should be re-verified before merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm which revision of test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py is on the branch and either run the probe (`tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --write-catalog`) for 5.5 or drop the calibrated-5.5 assertions.

findings.description: The evidence recorder treats `tool_input.active_skill` as a signal and writes `active_skill_seen_at` into `.run/platform-features.json`. The header text itself notes `tool_input` is model-authored. Since the recorder runs before the file_path check, any Write/Edit call (including non-App-Zone) carrying a fabricated `active_skill` field permanently stamps the evidence file.
findings.failure_mode: A model-emitted `active_skill` key produces a misleading 'platform supports active_skill' evidence record that an operator may read as grounds to enable `implement_gate.mode: authoritative`, at which point the gate trusts a model-controlled field.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the raw payload shape alongside the timestamp (e.g. top-level keys present) so a reviewer can distinguish a harness-set field from a model-authored one, and state in the evidence record that it is non-authoritative.
